definitions.gloss: being broke; short of money; being strapped for cash
definitions.explanation: A state of not having enough money, typically temporary. Commonly used in casual conversation, especially among younger people.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今月|こんげつ}→今月：00720_kongetsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{金欠|きんけつ}だ。
⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦ずっと→ずっと：00912_zutto⟧{金欠|きんけつ}⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いている→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: I've been broke ever since the trip.

examples.japanese: ⟦{給料日|きゅうりょうび}→給料日：27561_kyuuryoubi⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧{金欠|きんけつ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{外食|がいしょく}→外食：03024_gaishoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{控|ひか}えている→控える：10054_hikaeru⟧。
examples.english: I'm always short of money before payday, so I cut back on eating out.

notes:
A compound of {金|きん} (money, gold) and {欠|けつ} (lack, shortage). The jocular {金欠病|きんけつびょう} ("money-deficiency disease") treats being broke as an illness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {金欠|きんけつ}だ (to be broke)
- {金欠|きんけつ}⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧ (state of being broke)
- {金欠|きんけつ}{病|びょう} (the "disease" of being broke, humorous)
- ⟦ずっと→ずっと：00912_zutto⟧{金欠|きんけつ} (perpetually broke)

REGISTER:
Casual; not for formal or business contexts. It describes a temporary personal shortage, not real poverty.
